summary: Anne M. Blackburn works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied as a graduate student at the University of Chicago in 1991. She held posts at Cornell University (c. 2001) and Harvard University, and is a Pali Text Society representative (attested 2026).

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Lambert Schmithausen, Karin Preisendanz, and others. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Hamburg, and University of Vienna.

Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. Her career includes posts at Smith College (1988–1989), Tokyo National Research Institute, and visiting scholar positions at Nara and Kyoto National Museums.

Anne Ruth Hansen specializes in Buddhist, religious, and historical studies, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She held an affiliation at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and serves as an Associate Professor and later Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Anne-Marie Blondeau works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Rolf Alfred Stein, Marcelle Lalou, and traditional teachers including Dagpo Rinpoche. Her career includes posts as editorial consultant and scholar at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1982, 2003).

Anne-Marie Esnoul (1908–1996) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Masson-Oursel, Nadine Stchoupak, and Sylvain Lévi. She served at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne and École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist. She pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg (c. 1957–1960), Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annelies Kammenhuber (1922–1995) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. under Ferdinand Sommer at the University of Hamburg. Her career included posts at Hamburg, the Pontifical Biblical Institute, and the University of Munich.

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) studied Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and religion at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg under Friedrich Heiler. She held professorial appointments at Marburg, Ankara University, the University of Bonn, and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) worked in Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Peking University. Her posts included teaching at Ankara University, Humboldt University, and apl. Professor at the University of Hamburg (1949–1966).

Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher. She earned degrees from the University of Otago and Somerville College, Oxford. She taught in the philosophy departments at Carnegie Mellon University (c. 1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (c. 1979–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed studies at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned a doctoral degree at the University of Vienna in 2002, having studied under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen works in Indology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, later holding research posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University, and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.
Annette Susannah Beveridge (1842–1929) worked in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and history. She was educated in London at Bedford College between 1858 and 1867.

Annie Barber Clarke (1861–1956) was an Indology scholar who studied at Radcliffe College (1883–1886) under Charles Rockwell Lanman. She held teaching positions at Parsons School and Miss Brown's School.

Annie Montaut specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Paris Cité, and Paris Nanterre, under Nicole Balbir. She held teaching posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Paris Nanterre, and INALCO.

Anshul Agarwal works in computational studies and Indology. He completed a Bachelor of Engineering at Vivekanand Education Society's Institute of Technology in 2014 and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur.

Antanas Poška (1903–1992) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Vytautas Magnus University (1926–1929), earned a B.A. from the University of Mumbai (1931–1933), and pursued doctoral studies at the University of Calcutta (c. 1931–1936).

Anthony C. Yu (1938–2015) was a scholar of sinology and religion. Educated at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. c. 1969), he served as a professor at the University of Chicago from c. 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Loyola University Chicago, Yale University, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2007), he held faculty positions at Transylvania University, Hobart and William Smith Colleges, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2016–2021).
